# Original static ELF fixtures

These original Apache-2.0 C sources produce small executable and shared-library
files for static inspection. No external firmware or SDK is included. The
compiler adds ordinary host startup/runtime references to the generated files;
those generated bytes are not checked into the source tree. Never run the
fixture executables.

From the source repository root, with the native Linux amd64 prerequisites
in the [build guide](../../build/README.md) satisfied, run:

```sh
make elf-fixtures
```

This checks the exact compiler version and writes fixtures under ignored
`dist/elf-fixtures/`. The underlying `build.sh` accepts one absolute output
directory beneath this checkout's `dist/`. It compiles the files and inspects
their metadata with `readelf`, without executing them.

Both roots contain an ET_EXEC executable and a shared library whose SONAME is
`libmaintenance.so.1`. SONAME is the name declared inside the library.
The candidate changes that library's bytes and adds `libextra.so.1` to the
executable's `DT_NEEDED` list of required libraries. The
`malformed/broken` fixture begins with ELF magic bytes but is deliberately
invalid.

Linux inventory tests build these fixtures automatically. They check metadata,
ELF files without section headers, category precedence and malformed-input
failures. Missing tools or compiler-version mismatches fail the tests rather
than skipping them. To run the full tests in Docker, follow
`make prepare-linux` with `make verify-linux` from the repository root.
